messages.content:
Given a question and an answer, analyze the complexity of each sentence in the answer. Break down each sentence into one or more fully understandable statements. Ensure that no pronouns are used in any statement. Format the outputs in JSON.
Please return the output in a JSON format that complies with the following schema as specified in JSON Schema:
{"properties": {"statements": {"description": "The generated statements", "items": {"type": "string"}, "title": "Statements", "type": "array"}}, "required": ["statements"], "title": "StatementGeneratorOutput", "type": "object"}Do not use single quotes in your response but double quotes,properly escaped with a backslash.

--------EXAMPLES-----------
Example 1
Input: {
    "question": "Who was Albert Einstein and what is he best known for?",
    "answer": "He was a German-born theoretical physicist, widely acknowledged to be one of the greatest and most influential physicists of all time. He was best known for developing the theory of relativity, he also made important contributions to the development of the theory of quantum mechanics."
}
Output: {
    "statements": [
        "Albert Einstein was a German-born theoretical physicist.",
        "Albert Einstein is recognized as one of the greatest and most influential physicists of all time.",
        "Albert Einstein was best known for developing the theory of relativity.",
        "Albert Einstein also made important contributions to the development of the theory of quantum mechanics."
    ]
}
-----------------------------

Now perform the same with the following input
input: {
    "question": "user: How does bot management work?\nassistant: Bot management works by identifying bots and distinguishing between desirable and undesirable bot behavior. This is done through various methods such as JavaScript challenges, CAPTCHA tests, behavioral analysis, and checking the reputation of the bot's IP address. Once identified, bad bots can be blocked, redirected, or rate limited, while good bots can be allowed or even served alternative content. Bot management also involves analyzing bot behavior and adding good bots to allowlists. Additionally, bot managers may use the robots.txt file to set up honeypots to identify and block bad bots.\nuser: What is CIS?\nassistant: CIS (Cloudflare Information Security) is a division of Cloudflare that collects data from requests flowing through its network every day. Utilizing this data, along with Cloudflare's machine learning and behavior analysis, CIS can identify potential bot activity. Additionally, it provides guidance on how to allow or disallow specific bot traffic using Firewall Rules.\nCloudflare offers a fast, highly performant, reliable, and secure internet service for customers operating on IBM Cloud. It provides three main capabilities to enhance your workflow: security, reliability, and performance. You can navigate to the features for each of these capabilities once you access the CIS user interface (UI).\nuser: CIS Architecture\nassistant: I don't have specific information about the architecture of CIS .\nuser: CIS workload insolation\nassistant: IBM Cloud and Cloudflare provide Cloud Internet Services (CIS) that ensure workload isolation by maintaining separate zones and domains for different customers within individual subaccounts in the CIS account at Cloudflare. Access to these accounts and the CIS control plane infrastructure is strictly limited to essential maintenance personnel only. \nData stored at Cloudflare is encrypted, except in cases where public access is necessary, such as with DNS records. The data handling for your site is managed exclusively by Cloudflare, with all proxied traffic directed to an IP address owned by Cloudflare. This traffic is routed through Cloudflare’s Anycast network to the nearest data center capable of processing the request. \nFor a tutorial on deploying isolated workloads across multiple locations and zones, please visit Deploy isolated workloads across multiple locations and zones.\nuser: What is edge VCP?\nassistant: I do not know. \nuser: How can I create an endpoint gateway?\nassistant: You can create an endpoint gateway for an IBM Cloud® service that you wish to access on your private VPC network using the user interface (UI), command-line interface (CLI), or application programming interface (API).\nBefore you begin, it's important to review the section on planning for virtual private endpoint gateways. After the endpoint gateway is created, you can modify the security groups associated with it, such as applying specific security group rules to the data paths of the endpoint gateway.\nuser: What do you do to configure ACLs for use with Endpoint Gateways?\nassistant: To configure Access Control Lists (ACLs) for use with Endpoint Gateways, it is best to do this before performing any actions on a virtual private endpoint (VPE), such as creating or updating it. The ACL is applied to the subnet containing the reserved IP linked to the endpoint gateway, which creates the VPE. Please ensure that the same rule is applied to each subnet with an endpoint connected to the VPE. This can be accomplished by using the same ACL across all the subnets or by establishing a rule in each of the different ACLs for the same VPE if they are located on different subnets.\nuser: Accessing virtual private endpoints",
    "answer": "You can access Virtual Private Endpoint (VPE)-enabled IBM Cloud services over a private network:\n\n- **From an on-premises network:** use IBM Cloud Direct Link. [S3]\n- **From another VPC:** use IBM Cloud Transit Gateway. [S3]\n\nAn endpoint gateway keeps traffic between your VPC and IBM Cloud services on the private network. [S3]\n\nIBM Cloud VPE for VPC lets you remotely access supported services using IP addresses of your choice, allocated from a subnet within your VPC. [S4]"
}
Output:

statements: Virtual Private Endpoint (VPE)-enabled IBM Cloud services can be accessed over a private network.
Virtual Private Endpoint (VPE)-enabled IBM Cloud services can be accessed from an on-premises network using IBM Cloud Direct Link.
Virtual Private Endpoint (VPE)-enabled IBM Cloud services can be accessed from another virtual private cloud (VPC) using IBM Cloud Transit Gateway.
An endpoint gateway keeps traffic between a virtual private cloud (VPC) and IBM Cloud services on the private network.
IBM Cloud VPE for VPC enables remote access to supported services using user-selected IP addresses.
The user-selected IP addresses are allocated from a subnet within the user's virtual private cloud (VPC).
